The streets of #NewDelhi echoed today with the voices of Tibetan exiles and supporters, as hundreds gathered to protest the visit of Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi for the 24th round of border talks with India. What Beijing hoped would be a quiet diplomatic engagement was met instead with a fierce reminder that Tibet’s struggle for freedom cannot be silenced.

Carrying the Tibetan national flag (banned in occupied Tibet but defiantly raised here), protesters condemned Wang Yi as the face of Beijing’s lies, repression, and colonial rule. Placards read “Free Tibet”, “China Out of Tibet”, and “Wang Yi Go Back”, turning the capital into a stage of resistance against Chinese authoritarianism.

Tibetans shouted slogans denouncing China’s occupation of Tibet since 1950, Beijing’s destruction of monasteries, mass surveillance, and forced boarding schools that tear Tibetan children from their culture. Many drew direct parallels between China’s ongoing border aggression against India and its decades-long military occupation of Tibet, calling both part of the same imperial expansion project.

China’s duplicity with Tibet is not an isolated case. Around the globe, nations are waking up to the cost of Beijing’s broken promises:

🔴#Philippines recently stood its ground in the South China Sea, successfully pushing back Chinese ships in contested waters. Manila has learned the hard way that Beijing’s “peaceful rise” masks coercion and bullying.

🔴#Italy is now moving to curb Chinese stakes in strategic companies, fearing infiltration into sensitive sectors like infrastructure and high-tech manufacturing.

🔴#EuropeanUnion has slapped restrictions on Chinese banks and investments, wary of Beijing’s growing economic leverage.

🔴#UnitedStates continues to warn allies of the dangers of overdependence on Chinese technology, blocking Beijing-linked companies from sensitive sectors.

🔴#Japan and #Australia have both tightened security ties with India and the U.S., directly citing China’s aggression as the driving force.

What unites these actions is a growing recognition that China cannot be taken at its word. The “peace” it sells is merely a pause before the next expansion.

The timing of Wang Yi’s visit could not be more controversial. While China’s state media paints the border talks as a step toward “stability,” India’s security forces remain locked in tense standoffs with Chinese troops along the Line of Actual Control (#LAC). Tibetans argue that the root of the conflict lies in China’s illegal annexation of Tibet, which once served as a peaceful buffer between the two #Asian giants.

International human rights groups have also warned that Tibet is facing one of the world’s most severe crackdowns. Freedom House rates Tibet as the least free place on earth, alongside Syria. More than 160 Tibetans have self-immolated since 2009 in desperate protest against #Chineserepression, acts of sacrifice largely ignored by global powers wary of offending Beijing.
